newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-LucasVarity Q1 ahead despite stg woes.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-LucasVarity Q1 ahead despite stg woes.

text.p: Anglo-American engineering giant LucasVarity Plc delivered a bumper 16 percent rise in first quarter pretax profits on Thursday and predicted a year of "modest top-line growth" despite continued pain from the strong pound.
The car components to aerospace group saw pretax profits for the first three months to April 30 in line with market forecasts at 72 million pounds ($117.6 million) against 62 million last year.
LucasVarity shares were generally cheered by the news, rising four pence to 208 by 1130 GMT.
"It looks pretty steady as she goes but it does mean numbers are beginning to come through to show that they can do what they said they are going to do," Lehman analyst Charles Armitage said.
Sales were up 8.6 percent to 1.21 billion pounds despite a hit from the strong pound which wiped 50 million pounds off the translation value of sales during the period.
LucasVarity chief executive Victor Rice remained upbeat.
"Against a background of mixed trading conditions and the strength of sterling, the first quarter results were a creditable start to the year."
Looking ahead, Rice said that despite the currency woes the first quarter performance "encourages us to believe that LucasVarity is on track to deliver modest top-line growth this year".
Margins are also seen improving further. In the first quarter they rose to 7.1 percent from 6.9 percent last year.
The figures were based on proforma combined results for the former British Lucas Industries and Varity Corp of the U.S. which merged in September 1996 to create LucasVarity.

The merger created one of the world's top 10 auto component suppliers. At the full year result stage in April Rice unveiled a clarified dividend policy which he said would combine a rolling share buyback programme, starting with a three percent buyback, with dividend growth.
But analysts said the ability to deliver the two in tandem hinged on whether there was a turnaround in difficult markets, citing a sluggish Europe in particular.
The latest trading update said European and North American automotive markets were to be flat for the rest of the year.
But "within Europe, the Italian, Spanish and UK markets are expected to outperform last year whilst the French market continues to be weak," it said.

The North American light truck sector, where the group has a leading presence, is seen showing continued good growth. Diesel engine markets are seen as mostly robust together with commercial aerospace. ($ = 0.612 British Pounds)
